title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: IMANI'S DRIP
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Imani Brooks, a house painter from Chattanooga, Tennessee.
Fourteen years on the job, and a paint stripe on all her pants.
Then one dripping can talked her into becoming an inventor.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DRIP
segments.quote: You see, but you do not observe.
segments.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
lines: One July morning, paint ran down the can, onto a customer's white porch. Four hundred dollars, gone.
That night, in an old Sherlock Holmes story by Arthur Conan Doyle, she read:
You see, but you do not observe.
Fourteen years she had wiped that drip, and never asked why.
She sketched a little pour spout on a paint stirrer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: PRACTICE SHOTS
segments.quote: An inventor fails nine hundred ninety-nine times, and if he succeeds once, he's in. He treats his failures simply as practice shots.
segments.author: Charles Kettering
lines: In the garage, spout number nine sprayed the cat. Number twenty glued itself to her thumb.
Her husband taped up a line from Charles Kettering, who helped invent the car's electric starter:
An inventor fails nine hundred ninety-nine times, and if he succeeds once, he's in. He treats his failures simply as practice shots.
So she wrote Shot twenty-one on the next one, and kept shooting.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ONE PIECE
segments.quote: Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
segments.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
lines: Shot thirty-one finally worked. It had eleven parts and two springs.
Her neighbor, a retired machinist, read her a line from the French pilot Antoine de Saint-Exupéry:
Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
She threw out all she could. What was left was one bent piece of steel. No drips.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE VAN
segments.quote: I got my start by giving myself a start.
segments.author: Madam C. J. Walker
lines: A big paint company in Atlanta said, Cute. Call us when you have customers.
She thought of Madam C. J. Walker, who went from washing laundry to running her own hair care company:
I got my start by giving myself a start.
She made fifty spouts at home and sold them from her van. Gone in a week.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CHEAP WAY
segments.quote: There are no shortcuts to any place worth going.
segments.author: Beverly Sills
lines: Then a factory offered plastic spouts at a quarter of the cost, if she signed today.
Her mom's fridge had a line from the opera singer Beverly Sills:
There are no shortcuts to any place worth going.
The plastic one cracked in two days. She said no, and found a small steel shop instead.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: TUESDAY NIGHTS
segments.quote: The reward for work well done is the opportunity to do more.
segments.author: Jonas Salk
lines: By spring, a hardware chain ordered ten thousand. She planned a very long nap.
Her neighbor handed her a line from Jonas Salk, the doctor behind the polio vaccine:
The reward for work well done is the opportunity to do more.
Now, on Tuesday nights, she opens her garage. A plumber, a nurse and a guy with a better mop bring drawings.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Look closer. Keep shooting. Cut the extras. Start yourself. Skip the shortcut. Do more.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Look closer. Keep shooting. Cut the extras. Start yourself. Skip the shortcut. Then do more.
I invented a sandwich once. It had already been invented.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
